list.name: service
list.description: Filters the JVM panels below - matters once more than one instance of the app-server reports under this tenant.

options.content:
__BUDGET_TABLE__

Rendered from the manifest at generation time - not a live query. See **Ingestion Budget Usage** alongside for the live percentage.

panels.title: Ingestion Budget Usage (per Signal)
panels.description: This tenant's real ingested volume since local midnight (Europe/Zurich), as a percentage of EACH signal's own daily budget - Metrics (Mimir), Logs (Loki), Traces (Tempo), Profiles (Pyroscope) each shown as its own line. Both values read directly from two gauges scripts/ingestion-midnight-snapshot.py pushes every 2 minutes (demo_ingestion_since_midnight, demo_ingestion_daily_budget) - no subtraction on this panel's own side (NFR-05 SECOND pre-test audit round, fixed here: this used to recompute "current minus a separately-pushed day-start snapshot" in this panel's OWN PromQL, independently of - and able to silently disagree with - the enforcer's own decision, with its own version of that script's pre-fix reset-insensitivity; both now read the exact same, already-correct value). Green below 80%, yellow 80-90%, red above 90%. Same formula as the Operator: Tenant Ingestion Budget dashboard's own panel, filtered to this one tenant. Queried via the Mimir-anonymous datasource, not __DATASOURCE_MIMIR__ - see README.md's Multi-Tenancy section for why (self-monitoring metrics land under the anonymous tenant).

panels.title: GC Load (time spent in GC)
panels.description: sum(rate(jvm_gc_duration_seconds_sum[...])) - the fraction of wall-clock time the JVM spends paused in garbage collection. Sustained values well above a few percent are worth investigating. Fixed 5m window, not $__rate_interval - found live (back when this was a separate jvm-middleware dashboard) that Mimir returns empty results for sum/max-by aggregations over a short rate() window on this tenant's high-cardinality JVM metrics (likely a query-sharding edge case), even though the bare unaggregated rate() works fine at any window size.

panels.title: Request Rate by Endpoint/Operation
panels.description: traces_spanmetrics_calls_total, generated automatically by Tempo's metrics-generator from real spans - no separate app instrumentation needed for this panel. Fixed 5m rate window (see GC Load's panel description for why a fixed window is used instead of $__rate_interval on span-derived metrics).

panels.title: Request Latency (p95) by Endpoint/Operation
panels.description: Also derived automatically from real spans via traces_spanmetrics_latency_bucket.

panels.title: Recent Traces
panels.description: A table, not the "traces" panel type - found live that Grafana's traces panel silently renders zero rows when Tempo's search response omits durationMs (which it does for very fast, sub-millisecond traces, e.g. this app's HelloWorld-servlet-speed requests), even though the underlying data is there. A table shows the same rows regardless.

panels.title: Recent Logs
panels.description: Queries by service_name, not k8s_namespace_name - this application runs on a VM, not a Kubernetes pod. Includes both the app's own OTLP-pushed logs and the app-server's own log files (e.g. Tomcat's catalina.out/access log via the filelog/tomcat receiver in instrumentation/middleware/tomcat/collector-config.yaml, pushed straight to the gateway - not the platform's own collector) - both report under this same tenant now (previously split into a separate middleware tenant; merged since this app-server is only ever used by this one application).
